newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 6.

text.p: Contract on murder accused -- lawyer: The youth accused of murdering a Naenae bank teller during an armed robbery has been moved to a more secure cell at Rimutaka Prison after guards found a hole in the prison fence near his cell. Page 1.

NZ First still to get extra MPs in Cabinet: NZ First will get another three MPs in the Cabinet next year, Prime Minister Jim Bolger has promised, despite the party's dismal performance so far. Page 2.

Peters to front at party meetings: NZ First leader Winston Peters is expected to front up to a series of closed regional party meetings starting this weekend as party members focus on party's performance and the actions of MP Tukoroirangi Morgan. Page 2.

Morgan own judge, says Bolger: If the Serious Fraud Office cleared NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan of fraud or impropriety then it would be up to Morgan to determine whether he had acted with integrity, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Monday night. Page 2.

Dairy Board executives to appear in court again: Dairy Board chairman Sir Dryden Spring said the board had not been told which British court its six executives would appear in when they made their second appearance on fraud charges this week. Page 2.

Compliance costs targeted: The Cabinet on Monday approved a sweeping review of internal government processes aimed at cutting compliance costs -- a hot issue raised frequently by the business community in recent months. Page 15.

BNZ makes 75 redundant; more may go: Seventy-five Bank of New Zealand workers had been made redundant as a result of the bank's reorganisation begun last year, a BNZ spokesman said on Monday. Page 15.

FCL plans to share Brunei oilfield stake: Fletcher Challenge plans to sell half its stake in two offshore Brunei oil exploration blocks, one containing a potentially large field of up to a billion barrels of oil. Page 15.

Busang gold 'bonanza' a scam -- consultants: The Indonesian jungle tract touted by Bre-X Minerals as one of the biggest gold bonanzas ever is instead the site of one biggest scams in the history of mining, an independent testing company alleged on Monday. Page 15.

Carrick gold samples prove encouraging for Summit: Gold samples from initial testing at the Carrick project in Central Otago suggested a similar mineralisation to that at Otago gold field Macraes, Summit Gold chief geologist Ian Mulholland said. Page 15.
Canadian company joins exploration bid: Vancouver-based CVL Resources has taken a half share in a petroleum exploration permit application in central Wairarapa. Page 15.
